clue.text: Tube carrying rainwater — shut up if inverted?

indicators.note: inverted asks for the two halves of the phrase to swap ends, the back part brought round to the front

parts.note: to tell someone to be quiet is to say 'pipe down'

explanation.surface: A rainwater pipe gets blocked when turned the wrong way up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if inverted' swaps the two words of PIPE DOWN rather than turning letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the vertical pipe that runs from a roof gutter to a drain, carrying rainwater down.

clue.text: Very much sooner than expected, daughter comes first

indicators.note: comes first puts the daughter at the front

parts.note: early means sooner than due

explanation.surface: A daughter arrives ahead of schedule and takes priority.
explanation.definitionFit: As in loved dearly, the adverb means greatly or very much.

clue.text: One of those placed in recollection of the war?

definitions.text: One of those placed in recollection of the war?

indicators.note: read as re-collection, the letters of the war are gathered again in a new order

explanation.surface: Something laid at a memorial to remember fallen soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds the answer: recollection as re-collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring-shaped arrangements of poppies are laid at memorials on Remembrance Sunday to honour the war dead.

clue.text: Dowdy type bedding fool, a reflective character appearing blue

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the whole run reads backwards
bedding means taking into bed, so the dowdy word holds the others inside

parts.note: a frump is a dowdy person
a sap is a fool

explanation.surface: A frumpy person sleeps with a fool, then broods on it, looking depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bedding' puts SAPA inside FRUMP to give FRUMSAPAP, and 'reflective' turns that round. Papa Smurf is the white-bearded leader of the blue cartoon Smurfs.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded elder of the Smurfs is a cartoon character with blue skin.

clue.text: What Toulouse-Lautrec would do to get thinner, say?

definitions.meaning: the French painter depicted cabaret dancers, so he might depict a woman who undresses on stage
a solvent like a thinner used to remove old coats from wood

explanation.definitionFit: A painter of Paris dancers would portray an exotic dancer; the phrase is also a chemical for removing old coats from woodwork.

clue.text: Leader from Gujarat with an appropriate garment, testament demanding freedom?

definitions.text: Leader from Gujarat with an appropriate garment, testament demanding freedom?

indicators.note: the leading letter of the state name Gujarat is taken
the testament wants out, so its letters are released from the garment

parts.note: a dhoti, the loincloth he famously wore, suits this Indian leader
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: An Indian leader in fitting dress whose life was a testament to the struggle for independence.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: DHOTI loses OT to give DHI. He was born in Gujarat and led India's campaign for freedom from British rule.
explanation.definitionFit: The independence campaigner Mohandas, born in Porbandar in Gujarat, wore a simple dhoti and pursued freedom for India.

clue.text: Upper vertebra eventually cut

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: at last means eventually

explanation.surface: A top vertebra is finally severed.
explanation.definitionFit: The topmost bone of the spine, which supports the skull, carries the name of the Titan holding up the sky.

clue.text: Quarter of the pack ice

definitions.meaning: one of the four suits in a deck of cards
slang for jewels, especially gems that glitter

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a card suit, one of four, and gemstones known in slang as ice.

clue.text: Allusion contained by cryptic undone

parts.note: being contained by something is being in it

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling, so the letters are mixed into a riddle

explanation.surface: A hint hidden inside a puzzle that has come apart.
explanation.definitionFit: An indirect suggestion, often a suggestive hint, is an allusion.

clue.text: Theatre production's opening in a new capital

indicators.note: in places the letter from the production inside the city name

parts.note: New Delhi is India's capital

indicators.note: the opening of the word production's is its first letter

explanation.surface: A stage show premieres in a newly built capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Adelphi is a theatre on the Strand in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known West End playhouse on London's Strand bears this name.

clue.text: Again pick up on miscalculation in the end by Shakespearean character

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

indicators.note: in the end selects the final letter of miscalculation

explanation.surface: Someone has to take up a lesson again after an old king's misjudgement.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a skill is to learn it, so picking it up again is learning it afresh.

clue.text: Protest upsetting the Two Ronnies at times?

indicators.note: upsetting knocks the letters over into a new order

parts.note: two Ronnies are two RONs, Ron being short for Ronnie; the Two Ronnies were a BBC comedy double act
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that the BBC comedy pair sometimes caused offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Two Ronnies (Barker and Corbett) were a long-running British TV sketch show; here each Ronnie is just RON, and RONRON joins ATTIMES as the anagram pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A remonstrance or forceful objection is a protest, the noun form of remonstrate.

clue.text: Blooming fast car?

definitions.meaning: as a noun, a blooming is a flower, here the sacred water lily of Asia
a British sports car marque made in Norfolk

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an Asian water lily in flower and a famous British make of racing and sports car.

clue.text: Sound of a cat fed pinch of big, big tablet

indicators.note: fed means the cat's word takes the letter in, like food

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, so of a cat gives tom's

indicators.note: a pinch is a tiny amount, so only the first letter of big

parts.note: a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: A cat's noise as it is given a bit of a big pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a homophone signal but simply means TONE, placed after the cat's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone is a large slab of stone, a big tablet carved with the dead person's name.

clue.text: Gormless fashion leader, subtle clothes

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the subtle word dresses round the others

parts.note: muted colours are subtle ones
ton is an old word for fashion, as in bon ton
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: A dim fashion boss wears understated outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean stupid or dull-witted, the hyphenated word being an old British insult for a slow person.

clue.text: Spot marker in wild antelope, body far away

indicators.note: in places the spot marker inside the jumbled animal
wild means the animal's letters run free into a new order

parts.note: X marks the spot on a treasure map

explanation.surface: A spotted marking on an untamed antelope seen from a great distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' makes EOPLANET from ANTELOPE, and 'in' puts X inside it after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet orbiting a star other than the Sun is a celestial body very far from Earth.

clue.text: Two dummies in, one taking another out?

parts.note: an ass is a fool or dummy
the second dummy is another ass
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple of fools get together, one asking another out on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking out' suggests a date, but here it means killing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired killer takes out, or kills, another person, often a public figure.

clue.text: Wine without label in dish

indicators.note: in places the two short words inside the dish

parts.note: a pie is a dish
no means without, as in no sugar
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A wine with no label served inside a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a South African red grape variety, a cross of Pinot Noir and Cinsaut, and its wine.

clue.text: Resistance between fluid and solid, fluid in rock fits in

indicators.note: fluid means flowing and changeable, so the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Something seeps into a rock and fits snugly in its cracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluid' appears twice: first in the definition, then as the anagram signal for IN ROCK FITS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Drag caused by a fluid rubbing along a solid surface is the physics term for this resistance.

clue.text: Country where female and male animals reported?

indicators.note: reported means the words are as heard when spoken

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep and a gander a male goose

explanation.surface: A land where both sexes of farm creatures have been seen.
explanation.walkthrough: EWE GANDER, spoken, is the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a landlocked nation in East Africa.

clue.text: Cold back home at the farm

parts.note: fro means back, as in to and fro
a sty is where pigs live on a farm

explanation.surface: It turns chilly back at the farmhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy or covered with frost, and so very cold.

clue.text: Dubious approach with unknown inscription — questionable text?

indicators.note: the unknown is written into the jumbled letters
dubious means uncertain, so the letters fall into a doubtful new order

parts.note: y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An uncertain approach to a mysterious inscription on a doubtful document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dubious' makes APOCRPHA from APPROACH; 'inscription' writes Y into it.
explanation.definitionFit: These books of doubtful authenticity sit outside the accepted biblical canon, writings of questionable status.

clue.text: Star on Irish wheels

indicators.note: to wheel is to turn round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the on side in cricket is the leg side

explanation.surface: A celebrity riding around Ireland on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side. 'wheels' turns LEGIR round.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a bright blue supergiant in the constellation Orion.

clue.text: Supine competitor's arm

definitions.meaning: a person racing feet-first on their back on a small sled down an ice track
a weapon, here the German semi-automatic pistol

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a rider in the luge, a sport of lying back on a sled, and a famous German handgun.

clue.text: Tail behind first of spectators in grandstand

indicators.note: behind places the tail after the letter from spectators
first of selects the opening letter of spectators

parts.note: a tail is something that wags, a wagger

explanation.surface: A tail-ender trails behind the first spectator in the stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grandstand' is the verb: to show off for the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To grandstand is to show off, and to swagger is to strut in the same boastful way.

clue.text: Time in profit after speculation, capital spent

indicators.note: the capital or first letter is used up and gone

parts.note: winnings are what you gain from a bet

explanation.surface: A spell when gambling pays off, though the stake is used up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks financial but means the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a team's or batter's turn at the crease is a spell of time; it also means any period of activity.

clue.text: Indicator of provocation?

definitions.meaning: the pointer on a dial or gauge
deliberate goading or antagonism, as between rival teams

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a gauge's pointer and the bad feeling of provocation between rivals.

clue.text: Tuesday nights originally created for rocking

indicators.note: created means the letters are made into something new
originally takes the first letter of nights

explanation.surface: Tuesday nights were first set up for rock music.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rocking sways and is unstable, not firmly balanced.
